books.name: Whale Watching
books.focus: Not only · However · whereby · Hardly · Were it not

items.s: ___ only did we see three humpback whales on our school trip, but one of them leapt out of the water.
items.tip: Not only + question order (did we see) … but (also): a strong way to add a surprise.
items.say: Not only did we see three humpback whales on our school trip, but one of them leapt out of the water.
items.ask: Blank only did we see three humpback whales on our school trip, but one of them leapt out of the water.

items.s: Our guide explained that whales sing songs ___ can travel for hundreds of kilometres.
items.tip: that / which for things in a defining clause (no commas).
items.say: Our guide explained that whales sing songs that can travel for hundreds of kilometres.
items.ask: Our guide explained that whales sing songs blank can travel for hundreds of kilometres.

items.s: ___ loud the engine was, the whales didn't seem to mind.
items.tip: However + adjective = it doesn't matter how: however loud it was.
items.say: However loud the engine was, the whales didn't seem to mind.
items.ask: Blank loud the engine was, the whales didn't seem to mind.

items.s: We learned about a rule ___ boats must stay at least a hundred metres away.
items.tip: whereby = by which, according to which (a formal word for rules and systems).
items.say: We learned about a rule whereby boats must stay at least a hundred metres away.
items.ask: We learned about a rule blank boats must stay at least a hundred metres away.

items.s: Hardly ___ we put our cameras away when a baby whale appeared beside the boat.
items.tip: Hardly + had + subject + past participle … when: one thing happened just after another.
items.say: Hardly had we put our cameras away when a baby whale appeared beside the boat.
items.ask: Hardly blank we put our cameras away when a baby whale appeared beside the boat.

items.s: ___ it not for these rules, the whales might be frightened away from the bay.
items.tip: Were it not for = If it weren't for (a formal 'if' with inversion).
items.say: Were it not for these rules, the whales might be frightened away from the bay.
items.ask: Blank it not for these rules, the whales might be frightened away from the bay.

items.s: Several of us felt seasick, ___ nobody regretted going.
items.tip: yet / but = and in spite of this.
items.say: Several of us felt seasick, but nobody regretted going.
items.ask: Several of us felt seasick, blank nobody regretted going.

items.s: It was, ___ far, the best trip we've ever had.
items.tip: by far + superlative = much more than any other: by far the best.
items.say: It was, by far, the best trip we've ever had.
items.ask: It was, blank far, the best trip we've ever had.

books.name: The Mural Project
books.focus: came up with · Rather than · regardless · many of whom · Little did

items.s: When the old wall behind the sports hall began to crumble, the pupils came ___ with a plan.
items.tip: come up with = think of (an idea or a plan).
items.say: When the old wall behind the sports hall began to crumble, the pupils came up with a plan.
items.ask: When the old wall behind the sports hall began to crumble, the pupils came blank with a plan.

items.s: Rather ___ simply repaint it, they would turn it into a giant mural.
items.tip: Rather than + verb = instead of doing it.
items.say: Rather than simply repaint it, they would turn it into a giant mural.
items.ask: Rather blank simply repaint it, they would turn it into a giant mural.

items.s: Every class, ___ of age, was invited to design one section.
items.tip: regardless of = it doesn't matter (what age).
items.say: Every class, regardless of age, was invited to design one section.
items.ask: Every class, blank of age, was invited to design one section.

items.s: The younger children, ___ of whom had never painted on a wall before, were thrilled.
items.tip: many of whom = many of these children (whom after of for people).
items.say: The younger children, many of whom had never painted on a wall before, were thrilled.
items.ask: The younger children, blank of whom had never painted on a wall before, were thrilled.

items.s: ___ colour they chose, it had to match the theme of 'Our Town'.
items.tip: Whatever + noun = it doesn't matter which colour.
items.say: Whatever colour they chose, it had to match the theme of 'Our Town'.
items.ask: Blank colour they chose, it had to match the theme of 'Our Town'.

items.s: The paint was sealed with a special varnish so ___ to protect it from the rain.
items.tip: so as to + verb = in order to.
items.say: The paint was sealed with a special varnish so as to protect it from the rain.
items.ask: The paint was sealed with a special varnish so blank to protect it from the rain.

items.s: ___ did they know that a local newspaper would write about it.
items.tip: Little did they know = they had no idea (inversion: did they know).
items.say: Little did they know that a local newspaper would write about it.
items.ask: Blank did they know that a local newspaper would write about it.

items.s: The wall now attracts visitors from all ___ the region.
items.tip: from all over = from every part of.
items.say: The wall now attracts visitors from all over the region.
items.ask: The wall now attracts visitors from all blank the region.

books.name: The Climbing Wall
books.focus: whom · in case · let alone · Given · no fewer than

items.s: I'd always been scared of heights, so I was nervous ___ trying the new climbing wall.
items.tip: nervous about + -ing: nervous about trying.
items.say: I'd always been scared of heights, so I was nervous about trying the new climbing wall.
items.ask: I'd always been scared of heights, so I was nervous blank trying the new climbing wall.

items.s: My instructor, ___ I'd met only that morning, was incredibly patient.
items.tip: whom = the object form of who (I had met her). Who is fine in everyday English.
items.say: My instructor, whom I'd met only that morning, was incredibly patient.
items.ask: My instructor, blank I'd met only that morning, was incredibly patient.

items.s: She checked my harness twice, just in ___ it was loose.
items.tip: in case = to be safe if something happens.
items.say: She checked my harness twice, just in case it was loose.
items.ask: She checked my harness twice, just in blank it was loose.

items.s: At first I couldn't reach the second hold, ___ alone the top.
items.tip: let alone = and certainly not (the top is even harder).
items.say: At first I couldn't reach the second hold, let alone the top.
items.ask: At first I couldn't reach the second hold, blank alone the top.

items.s: ___ how frightened I'd been, reaching halfway felt like a huge victory.
items.tip: Given (that) = when you think about the fact that…
items.say: Given how frightened I'd been, reaching halfway felt like a huge victory.
items.ask: Blank how frightened I'd been, reaching halfway felt like a huge victory.

items.s: By the end of the month, I had reached the top ___ fewer than six times.
items.tip: no fewer than + number = as many as (it's surprising, a lot!).
items.say: By the end of the month, I had reached the top no fewer than six times.
items.ask: By the end of the month, I had reached the top blank fewer than six times.

items.s: It goes to show that fear needn't hold you ___.
items.tip: hold someone back = stop them from doing something.
items.say: It goes to show that fear needn't hold you back.
items.ask: It goes to show that fear needn't hold you blank.

items.s: I'm now saving ___ for a pair of proper climbing shoes.
items.tip: save up for = keep money until you can buy something.
items.say: I'm now saving up for a pair of proper climbing shoes.
items.ask: I'm now saving blank for a pair of proper climbing shoes.
